result.title: TNVD-SC: Diagnosing Scan Context Failures in Forests with Terrain-Normalized Vertical Distributions
result.summary: Long-term LiDAR place recognition in forests is difficult because repetitive vegetation and uneven terrain create severe structural aliasing. We diagnose Scan Context (SC) by separating candidate retrieval from fine matching: on the standardized TreeLoc++ Wild-Places protocol, a TNVD support key places a valid location in the top-25 set for approximately 99% of queries, while conventional SC matching on those candidates reaches only 61.84% mean R@1. With an identical raw-SC candidate set, terrain normalization improves max-height cells by only 1.21 points but vertical-distribution cells by 19.72 points. These observations motivate Terrain-Normalized Vertical Distribution Scan Context (TNVD-SC), which preserves the SC ring-sector topology while encoding terrain-relative vertical probability distributions. Under the standardized TreeLoc++ protocol, TNVD-SC reaches 91.83% mean R@1 and attains the highest R@1 mean and R@1 stability among the compared methods, while TreeLoc++ remains stronger in mean MR, MF1, and AUC. The unchanged method reaches 85.14% mean R@1 on the four-session CVTNet-style NCLT evaluation. A lossless count-coded implementation with exact hierarchical Jensen-Shannon search reduces descriptor payload by 3.86x and compute latency by 23.8% without changing the audited retrieval outputs.

AI.brief_summary: 在森林长期 LiDAR 位置识别中把候选检索与精细匹配分离，诊断 Scan Context 因植被重复与地形起伏产生的结构混叠，并提出保留环—扇区拓扑、改为编码地形相对垂直概率分布的 TNVD-SC，同时给出无损计数编码与分层 Jensen-Shannon 搜索以降低描述子体积与时延。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先粗检索候选、再精细匹配」的两阶段诊断与压缩式搜索，或可供核查 LVR 中证据获取（LOOK）与候选筛选的成本—收益权衡；但属机器人定位领域，迁移性需进一步确认。
